Left as explicit, *commented* discards after reading: `Session::fail`'s `set_state` (the guard is the same `allowed` matrix the transition uses, so it cannot fail), `clipboard_guest_link`'s `LINK.set` (single writer inside `get_or_init`), `amos-audio`'s condvar wait (only the elapsed time matters), `amos-clipboard`'s per-connection session, `mail.rs`'s demo seeding, and the gRPC stream frames to a client that disconnected. This file is a RATCHET: a file gaining a hand-written discard, or a new file appearing with one, fails `make lint` until the addition is acknowledged here; a file that drops below its count **fails** as a stale entry (REQ-A447: the ratchet must shrink, not rot — a note was not enough). Honest scope: the sites in the files listed above were read one by one, and the ones that hid a real failure were fixed; what is left is deliberate. `macroGenerated` is a snapshot for the reader — the gate prints the live count every run and does not ratchet it (nothing there is actionable). REQ-A187: the scan runs clippy **twice** (plain + every `android` feature), because a clippy-based gate cannot see `#[cfg(feature = "android")]` code at all; measured when added, 113 discard sites existed only in the featured pass and nine of them were real silent failures in the device path (dropped camera frame, unarmed glue bus, undelivered in-call/SMS events, unbound dial/sensor contexts, unwritten self-care report, dropped mic-permission reply) — each fixed by reporting the failure instead of discarding it. What remains above the old 62 is the deliberate `OnceLock::set` exactly-once pattern of the Android attaches, now counted here so the ratchet covers the device surface too. The two passes are de-duplicated by (lint, span) so a feature-independent warning is never counted twice.
